rules.rule_en: In Simple Present passive, use is/am/are + V3 (past participle).
In Present Continuous passive, use is/am/are + being + V3.
In Present Perfect passive, use has/have + been + V3.
In Past Continuous passive voice, use 'being' after the auxiliary verb.
In Past Perfect passive voice, use 'been' after 'had'.
In Simple Future passive voice, use 'be' after the modal 'will'.
Future Perfect Tense passive construction: Subject + will have been + past participle + by agent.
To convert Active Voice to Passive Voice, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence, often utilizing the auxiliary verb 'be' plus the past participle.

examples.note_en: Simple Past: I killed a snake -> A snake was killed by me.
Past Continuous: He was driving a car -> A car was being driven by him.
Past Perfect: They had completed the assignment -> The assignment had been completed by them.
Simple Future: She will buy a car -> A car will be bought by her.
Imperative sentence 'Help him' transforms to 'Let him be helped' in passive voice.
Simple present active 'Farmers sow maize' becomes 'Maize is sown' in passive.
Active: Spectators thronged the streets. Passive: The streets were thronged with spectators.
Active: Everyone will blame us. Passive: We will be blamed by everyone.
Active: The wind blew down the trees. Passive: The trees were blown down by the wind.
Active: The police caught the thieves. Passive: The thieves were caught by the police.
Active: You must do your duty. Passive: Your duty must be done by you.
Active: Someone has cleaned the windows. Passive: The windows have been cleaned.

translations.en: He sings a song.
A song is sung by him.
He does not sing a song.
A song is not sung by him.
Does he sing a song?
Is a song sung by him?
I am writing a letter.
A letter is being written by me.
I am not writing a letter.
A letter is not being written by me.
Am I writing a letter?
Is a letter being written by me?
She has finished her work.
Her work has been finished by her.
She has not finished her work.
Her work has not been finished by her.
Has she finished her work?
Has her work been finished by her?
Simple Past: I killed a snake / A snake was killed by me.
translations.ta: நான் ஒரு பாம்பைக் கொன்றேன் / ஒரு பாம்பு என்னால் கொல்லப்பட்டது.

translations.en: Past Continuous: He was driving a car / A car was being driven by him.
translations.ta: அவன் கார் ஓட்டிக் கொண்டிருந்தான் / கார் அவனால் ஓட்டப்பட்டுக் கொண்டிருந்தது.

translations.en: Past Perfect: They had completed the assignment / The assignment had been completed by them.
translations.ta: அவர்கள் அந்தப் பணியை முடித்திருந்தார்கள் / அந்தப் பணி அவர்களால் முடிக்கப்பட்டிருந்தது.

translations.en: Simple Future: She will buy a car / A car will be bought by her.
translations.ta: அவள் கார் வாங்குவாள் / கார் அவளால் வாங்கப்படும்.

translations.en: You will have started the job.
The job will have been started by you.
Help him.
Let him be helped.
Farmers sow maize in the rainy season.
Maize is sown in the rainy season.
Are you writing?
Is a letter being written by you?
The workers were digging a canal.
A canal was being dug by the workers.
I will finish the job by the end of this week.
translations.ta: இந்த வார இறுதிக்குள் நான் வேலையை முடிப்பேன்.

translations.en: The job will be finished by the end of this week.
The manager will give you a ticket.
You will be given a ticket by the manager.
Spectators thronged the streets.
The streets were thronged with spectators.
Everyone will blame us.
We will be blamed by everyone.
The wind blew down the trees.
The trees were blown down by the wind.
The police caught the thieves.
The thieves were caught by the police.
You must do your duty.
Your duty must be done by you.
Someone has cleaned the windows.
The windows have been cleaned.

p112: This page provides bilingual tables demonstrating the conversion of active voice sentences into passive voice across various tenses, including Future Perfect, along with examples for imperative and simple present/past continuous sentences.
